openings.claim: Use the first parent function: a removable guide retains the scraper through contact boundaries. Shape and drill the supplied steel strips only, bolt them through existing carriage slots, and provide side/end boundaries plus a loosenable keeper entirely away from the working edge and stroke clearance. This is a proposed configuration, not demonstrated retention.
openings.delta: Change the retention dependency from friction to geometric confinement carried by steel-strip boundaries. The action for removal is loosening the keeper and withdrawing by unmarked plate surfaces while the carriage stays on its rails. The nearest ordinary rival is a cork-padded screw clamp mounted through the same slots, relying on compression and friction.
openings.prediction: If the boundaries and keeper constrain every relevant escape direction, each plate should remain within 1 mm after twenty manual strokes, including the spare, and permit removal/return within sixty seconds with gloves. Unlike the friction clamp, movement should terminate at a boundary even when compression is absent. The magnets’ 3 N versus 7 N disparity alone does not establish a difference between these two mechanical configurations.
openings.probe: First check whether the slots and available strips permit complete confinement and keeper access outside the marked clearance. Stop fabrication if that cannot be achieved without forbidden modification. Within eighty fabrication minutes and twenty observation minutes, compare at most two configurations: guide and friction clamp. For each, run two twenty-stroke trials with the original plate and a final twenty-stroke trial with the spare; measure displacement against initial marks. Perform three removal/return checks per configuration, the final check with the spare and supplied gloves; time and observe edge avoidance. Record boundary contact versus clamp slip. Use the pull scale only within 10 N to explore escape directions; this cannot establish unprovided stroke loads.
assumptions: Slot spacing, carriage geometry and available strip length permit boundaries, keeper access and fastening without clearance intrusion; this indispensable feasibility is unspecified.

The strips and bolts resist manual-stroke loads; loads and bending capacity are unknown. Defeat conditions include strip flex, an unconstrained escape direction, displacement above 1 mm, inaccessible fasteners with gloves, or service exceeding sixty seconds.
A successful short probe supports only the stipulated manual task; no deployment or durability claim follows.

assessment: One uncertain guide opening. Its feasibility requires inspecting the supplied geometry; a run cap cannot supply missing confinement or capacity evidence.
